listening.title: Planning the follow-up email after a client meeting

lines.speaker: Nam (Sales Manager)
lines.text: Linh, how did the meeting with the client go yesterday afternoon?

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: Quite well. They liked the demo, but they want more details about the price.

lines.speaker: Nam (Sales Manager)
lines.text: Then send them the pricing sheet today, while the meeting is still fresh.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: I will. Should I also attach a case study from a similar company?

lines.speaker: Nam (Sales Manager)
lines.text: Yes, good idea. It helps them trust us and show something to their boss.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: They also asked if we can start with a small pilot before a full contract.

lines.speaker: Nam (Sales Manager)
lines.text: That is normal. Offer them a three-month trial with a clear success plan.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: Okay. Their procurement team will join the next call, so I need their availability.

lines.speaker: Nam (Sales Manager)
lines.text: Ask for two or three time slots in the same email thread.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: Got it. And I will use reply all so everyone stays in the loop.

lines.speaker: Nam (Sales Manager)
lines.text: Perfect. Please send it before five so they can read it this evening.
